judgements.reason: ContourIntegration is archived complete (the Hungerbühler–Wasem theorem, homology Cauchy theorem and argument principle are in TauCeti/Analysis/Contour), while OneParameterSemigroups still lacks the complexified resolvent-holomorphy bridge and the converse Stieltjes/Bernstein correspondences; both remaining gaps are small.

Spin still needs the identification of spin and half-spin modules as L(ω), which relies on Weyl-character theory not yet built, plus Spin₄/Spin₅/Spin₆ exceptional isomorphisms, Spin₈ triality (including lifting a diagram automorphism to the simply connected group) and general Kostant isotypy. OneParameterSemigroups lacks only complex resolvent analyticity and Stieltjes converses.

AutomorphicLFunctions must first build Schwartz–Bruhat analysis, Bruhat–Tits theory, smooth p-adic representations with Satake and Bernstein–Zelevinsky derivatives, Casselman–Wallach globalization and adelic cusp forms, none of which exists, and only then Tate, Godement–Jacquet and Rankin–Selberg integrals. Spin's remaining gaps (L(ω) identification, three exceptional isomorphisms, triality, Kostant isotypy) sit on largely built Clifford and Lie foundations.

Sieve methods build on Mathlib's Dirichlet L-functions and Selberg Λ² setup and add classical analytic layers: zero-free regions and Siegel–Walfisz, the large sieve, Bombieri–Vinogradov, Maynard weights and Chen/affine sieves. AutomorphicLFunctions needs an absent representation-theoretic foundation (smooth p-adic representations, Satake, Bruhat–Tits, Casselman–Wallach, adelic cusp forms), with Godement–Jacquet and Rankin–Selberg theory stacked on top.

Metaplectic needs the adelic automorphic foundation (reduction theory, (g,K)-modules, cusp forms, meromorphic continuation of Eisenstein series, smooth representations) and then Stone–von Neumann, the Weil index, local theta correspondence, global theta kernels and BFH analysis on the GSp(4) cover. The sieve roadmap's classical analytic stack builds on existing L-series and sieve APIs.

Faltings needs abelian schemes with duals and polarizations, Siegel moduli with integral compactifications, Néron models with semistable reduction, p-divisible groups with p-adic Hodge inputs, and Arakelov (Faltings) heights; the baseline has only abelian varieties over fields and naive heights. Metaplectic's automorphic foundation, Eisenstein continuation and theta/Weil-representation chain is comparably deep but smaller, and Mathlib's adeles and Fourier analysis support it in part.

GlobalShtukas needs the full ℓ-adic formalism (six operations, perverse sheaves, Weil II), stacks, Bruhat–Tits/Satake and function-field class field theory. It then builds classical geometric Satake, shtuka moduli with their intersection cohomology, Drinfeld's lemma, excursion reconstruction and L. Lafforgue's compactification and trace-formula proof. Faltings' declared inputs (abelian schemes, Siegel compactifications, Néron models, p-adic Hodge, Arakelov heights) are broader in recorded stages, but its own finiteness layers are thin.

Heegner consumes essentially the whole modularity edifice (modular curves over ℤ, Serre weights, deformation rings and patching, potential modularity, Faltings finiteness) and adds CM theory, Gross–Zagier, Kolyvagin systems, anticyclotomic Iwasawa theory and GU(2,2) congruences, with a recorded chain about 96 stages deep. GlobalShtukas' ℓ-adic/Weil II, geometric Satake and Lafforgue layers form a large but much narrower stack.

Heegner's modular parametrization requires EllipticCurveModularity, whose closure contains every SerreWeightAndLevelOptimisation layer, and it adds CM theory, Euler/Kolyvagin systems, Gross–Zagier inputs and anticyclotomic main conjectures. Serre optimization stops at level lowering and Edixhoven's theorem, built on modular and Shimura curves, Néron models and GL₂ automorphic inputs.

Excursion needs the full Fargues–Scholze geometry (diamonds, six operations, v-stacks, Bun_G, Satake on the B_dR-affine Grassmannian, parameter stacks and the spectral action), plus classical LLC for GL_n through the two-tower realization and Laumon–Rapoport–Stuhler D-elliptic sheaves. Serre optimization needs modular and Shimura curves over ℤ, Néron character groups, Jacquet–Langlands, modular Galois representations and integral p-adic Hodge theory; its recorded closure is similar in size, but its own level- and weight-optimization layers are thinner.

Excursion needs all of VStack's diamond and Bun_G sheaf theory plus geometric Satake, L-parameter stacks, Weil II, Shimura-variety realizations of LLC for GL_n and LRS. Overconvergent needs perfectoid Shimura varieties with the Hodge–Tate period map, canonical subgroups, Hilbert compactifications and weight spaces before the BHW construction, which is substantial but a much smaller body of theory.

PadicHodgeRegulators needs a whole K-theory branch (Quillen K-theory and spectra, K-theory of local fields, Suslin's K₃ and Bloch groups, motivic cohomology, Borel regulators), syntomic regulators, (φ,Γ)-modules with Perrin-Riou's big logarithm, and modular Galois representations at p, on top of p-adic Hodge foundations. Overconvergent shares the perfectoid and p-adic Hodge base but adds only perfectoid Shimura varieties, canonical subgroups, automorphic bundles and the BHW/AIP construction.

PadicHodgeRegulators' recorded inputs already contain most of the diamond étale-cohomology foundation, and it adds algebraic K-theory, motivic cohomology, syntomic regulators, (φ,Γ)-modules with Iwasawa cohomology, and modular Galois representations. VStack adds Fargues–Fontaine vector bundles, Bun_G and the FS IV/VII sheaf categories to the same diamond base.

Excursion consumes every VStack layer (VS1, VS2, VS4, VS5) and adds geometric Satake, Hecke stacks and local shtukas, L-parameter stacks with integral invariant theory, the spectral action, and the GL_n comparisons via the two-tower realization and LRS.
ContourIntegration is complete in Tau Ceti, whereas Spin still needs the L(ω) identification of spin modules, the Spin₄–Spin₆ exceptional isomorphisms, triality for Spin₈ and general Kostant isotypy.

GlobalShtukas needs the ℓ-adic six-functor formalism, perverse sheaves and Weil II, stacks, Bruhat–Tits/Satake and function-field class field theory, and then geometric Satake, shtuka cohomology, Drinfeld's lemma and both Lafforgue proofs. Metaplectic's automorphic foundation (reduction theory, cusp forms, Eisenstein continuation) with its Weil-representation and theta layers is a smaller, more analytic stack.

Heegner imports PadicHodgeRegulators' Bloch–Kato and Iwasawa layers (L0-L4) and also needs modularity of elliptic curves, Faltings finiteness, CM theory, Gross–Zagier, Euler/Kolyvagin systems and anticyclotomic main conjectures, in a recorded chain about 96 stages deep. PadicHodgeRegulators' extra K-theory and motivic branch (K-theory of local fields, Suslin's K₃, Borel regulators) is large but shallower, with a chain of about 48.

Both need abelian schemes, PEL/Siegel moduli with integral compactifications and p-adic Hodge/perfectoid inputs. Overconvergent adds perfectoid Shimura varieties with the Hodge–Tate period map, canonical subgroups, Hilbert modular varieties, automorphic bundles and weight spaces beneath the substantial BHW/AIP construction; Faltings adds Néron models and Arakelov heights beneath a thin finiteness layer.

Serre optimization needs, besides étale cohomology and the diamond and p-adic comparison foundations that appear among its recorded inputs, modular and Shimura curves over ℤ, Néron character groups, GL₂ automorphic theory with Jacquet–Langlands, Weil II, and modular Galois representations with local–global compatibility. VStack needs the perfectoid–diamond–Fargues–Fontaine–Bun_G stack with the FS IV/VII categories on top.

Heegner needs modularity of elliptic curves, CM theory, Galois cohomology with Poitou–Tate duality, Euler systems, Gross–Zagier and Iwasawa main conjectures, none of which is in the baseline. The sieve roadmap needs classical analytic layers (PNT error terms, Siegel–Walfisz, the large sieve, Bombieri–Vinogradov, Maynard, Chen) over Mathlib's L-series and Selberg sieve.

Both need smooth p-adic representations, (g,K)-modules and adelic automorphic forms. Metaplectic additionally needs meromorphic continuation of Eisenstein series and a long metaplectic chain (Stone–von Neumann, Weil index, local theta, global theta kernels, half-integral weight, Eisenstein analysis on the GSp(4) cover), and it imports AL.0 itself. AutomorphicLFunctions' own extras are Bruhat–Tits/Satake, Bernstein–Zelevinsky derivatives and the Tate, Godement–Jacquet and Rankin–Selberg integrals.

VStack needs the perfectoid–diamond–six-functor foundation, the relative Fargues–Fontaine curve and Bun_G, and its recorded chain is deeper, but its own layers are the FS IV/VII sheaf categories. GlobalShtukas needs ℓ-adic six operations, perverse sheaves, Weil II, stacks and Bruhat–Tits/Satake, then geometric Satake, shtuka cohomology, Drinfeld's lemma and both Lafforgue proofs, which amount to more new theory.

Faltings needs abelian schemes and their moduli with integral compactifications, Néron models, p-divisible groups with p-adic Hodge inputs, and Arakelov heights, a deep arithmetic-geometry stack. AutomorphicLFunctions needs smooth p-adic representations with Satake, Casselman–Wallach globalization and cusp forms before the Tate, Godement–Jacquet and Rankin–Selberg integrals, a large but shallower representation-theoretic stack.

Beyond the shared abelian-scheme, Shimura-variety and p-adic Hodge base, Serre optimization needs modular curves over ℤ, Néron character groups, Shimura curves with Čerednik–Drinfeld uniformization, GL₂ automorphic theory with Jacquet–Langlands, Weil II, and modular Galois representations with local–global compatibility. Overconvergent adds only perfectoid Shimura varieties, canonical subgroups, automorphic bundles and weight spaces.
